28506.description:
Engineer, Ventilation & Projects - Underground


About Us


New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. Our commitment to safety, innovation, and responsible mining ensures that we not only contribute to the economy but also support the development and prosperity of the regions we operate in. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.


 


The New Porgera Limited now has a vacancy for a qualified and experienced individual to join our Mine Technical Services Department as an 
Engineer, Ventilation & Projects Underground
.


 


About the role


Reporting to the Superintendent - Underground, the Engineer, Ventilation & Projects Underground is responsible for design, monitoring, optimization and continuous improvement of underground ventilation systems, while also delivering engineering projects that support safe, efficient and compliant underground operations.


 


In this role, you will be responsoble for: 


Ventilation
 Engineering






Design, implement and maintain underground ventilation systems to ensure safe working environment






Monitor airflow, gas levels, dust, heat and diesel particulate matter (DPM)






Conduct ventilation surveys, audits and modelling






Conduct ventilation surveys, audits and modelling






Review and update ventilation plans, schematics and reports






Investigate ventilation-related incidents and recommend corrective actions






Ensure compliance with statutory ventilation and health and safety requirements






Project Engineering






Plan and deliver underground engineering projects, including ventilation upgrades, infrastructure improvements and systems optimizations






Prepare project scopes, schedules, budgets and risk assessments






Coordinate contractors, suppliers and internal stakeholders






Manage project execution, commissioning and handover






Track project performance and report progress to management






Maintain a high level of health and safety awareness and comply with the NPL Occupational Health & Safety Policy and all health and safety rules and procedures






 


About You


To succeed in this role, the ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications and experiences:






Tertiary Qualifications in Mine Engineering, or related






Experience working in Underground Mining environment






Strong understanding of underground ventilation principles






Knowledge of relevant mining legislation and safety standards






Competency in ventilation monitoring and reporting tools






Strong analytical, problem -solving and communication skills






Experience in ventilation modelling software ( e.g. Ventsim)






Project management experience






Experience in contract management






 


Working Conditions






Underground work environment with rotating or fixed shift roster






Exposure to typical mining conditions – confined spaces, noise, dust and variable temperatures






Use of PPE and adherence to all safety protocols required






Mobilization Requirement 


In return, you will be joining a world-class mining operation with the opportunity to impact the development and upskilling of our predominantly local workforce, combined with a team keen to learn and absorb knowledge. This offers a unique opportunity to further shape the department and improve NPL’s social performance and people knowledge.


 


You will be joining an operation that values safety and lead a team towards best-in-class safety practices whilst contributing to the development of a highly capable national workforce, making a lasting impact on the industry.


This role is offered on a FIFO basis with a 21/14 roster and a highly competitive remuneration package.


 


Note
: This advert will be open until
 25th of September ,2026
. If you do not hear from NPL within two (2) weeks of this date, please consider your application unsuccessful for this opportunity
.






Apply

28500.description:
Job Type:
 
Permanent
 
About us 


K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate. 


We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.


About the role


Complete all work that is required in the underground mining environment. This is inclusive of but not limited to grouting, water and air installation, scaling and barring, installation of other mine services, drilling requirements to be used Air leg and Rock Drills.


Key / Major Accountabilities


Key accountabilities of this position include.




The pumping of cement into drilled holes to stabilize ground support.


Lifting of mixing equipment into workbasket.


Cleaning of equipment and vehicle after use.


The wash down and scaling / barring of loose rocks from the walls and backs of an underground tunnel 


Roll out water hoses from services to broken rock.


Install cable bolts into drill holes in backs of underground tunnel that are used for extra ground support.




About You


To be considered for this role, it is essential that you are physically strong and healthy and have minimum Grade 10 level of education. In addition to this you will have some or all the following.




Minimum 1 year experience in underground mine work environment.


Ability to read and write in both Tok Pisin and English.


Be always very safety conscious and be able to identify risks.


Must be a local from Mine impact areas.




Life at K92  


K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.


Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.


At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.


In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster. 


THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP 






Apply

Reinhold Engineering and Group of Companies Limited is a nationally owned civil works and building construction company based in Port Moresby. As we continue to grow and strengthen our operations across Papua New Guinea, we are seeking a capable and experienced Accounts Officer with proven experience in the construction industry to support our administrative functions.


 


About the Role


The Accounts Officer will be responsible for maintaining financial records, processing daily transactions, and ensuring the fiscal health and compliance of our Company. The successful incumbent will support accounts payable/receivable, reconciling ledgers and handle financial reporting.


This position is well suited to an individual who is organized, confidential, and capable of operating in a fast-paced construction and project-based environment.


 


Key Responsibilities




Provide administrative support across all finance functions.


Accurately record and process all daily financial transactions, including vendor invoices, employee expenses, and customer payments.


Perform routine reconciliation of bank statements, accounts payable, accounts receivable and cash book ledgers to ensure there are no discrepancies.


Prepare and send out invoices/bills, track accounts, and follow up with clients on overdue payments.


Provide accurate summaries, data and reports for month-end and year-end close.


Verify transaction documentation and ensure all records comply with company policies, tax laws and financial regulations.


Maintain and update confidential reconciliation, transactions and bank statements and assist with audits as required.


Other duties in line with the role as requested by management.

Bachelor’s degree or Diploma in Accounting

Strong proficiency in MS Office Applications specifically MS Excel


Excellent communication and reporting skills

High attention to detail

Position: 
Project Manager
Company: 
Reinhold Engineering and Group of Companies Limited
Location: 
Port Moresby


 


Reinhold Engineering and Group of Companies Limited is a nationally owned civil works and building construction company based in Port Moresby. As we continue to grow and strengthen our operations across Papua New Guinea, we are seeking a capable and experienced Project Manager to lead, manage and deliver on our multiple project sites.


 


About the Role


The Project Manager will oversee the entire lifecycle of multiple projects. Be responsible for directing on-site teams, managing all project resources, and maintaining rigorous compliance with safety and environmental protocols. The role’s main objective is to deliver exceptional results that align with client expectations, company standards, and strategic business goals.


 


Key Responsibilities


Project Leadership & Execution




Develop comprehensive project plans, schedules, and budgets, and manage their execution from concept to completion.


Lead and coordinate multidisciplinary teams, including engineers, contractors, and subcontractors, to achieve project milestones.


Conduct regular site visits and meetings to monitor progress, resolve issues, and ensure alignment with project objectives.


Manage project scope, identify potential risks, and implement effective mitigation strategies.


Prepare and present detailed project reports for stakeholders and senior management.


Ensure project targets and deadlines are met as per instructed by General Manager inline with client requirements.




 


Resource & Financial Management




Create and maintain detailed resource schedules for personnel, equipment, and materials.


Monitor project expenditures against the approved budget, forecasting costs and implementing cost-control measures.


Review and approve vendor invoices, change orders, and other financial documentation.


Optimize resource allocation to maximize efficiency and productivity across all project phases.




 


Quality, Safety & Compliance




Establish and enforce stringent quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) procedures.


Ensure all project activities adhere to safety regulations and environmental laws.


Promote a culture of safety excellence, conducting regular audits and safety briefings with the on-site team.


Secure all necessary permits and ensure project documentation meets all regulatory standards.




 


Qualifications and Experience


Education & Certification




Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, construction management, or a related field.


Professional Engineer (PE) license is strongly preferred.


Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or equivalent is a significant advantage.




 


Experience




Minimum of 7+ years of progressive experience in civil engineering or construction project management.


Proven track record of successfully managing medium to large-scale civil infrastructure projects (e.g., roadways, utilities, site development, public works).


Demonstrated experience with project management software (e.g., MS Project, Primavera P6) and BIM tools.


Extensive hands-on experience managing subcontractors, negotiating contracts, and controlling project budgets.




 


Essential Skills & Competencies




Exceptional leadership and team management abilities, with a focus on mentoring and developing talent.


Superior communication, negotiation, and client relationship management skills.


Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a keen attention to detail.


In-depth knowledge of construction methods, materials, and legal regulations.


Ability to read and interpret complex engineering drawings, blueprints, and specifications.


Proficiency in standard office software suites and industry-specific applications.

Job Type:
 
Permanent
 
About us 


K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate. 


We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.


About the role


Responsible for operating the Underground Loader in a safe and appropriate manner to carry out earth moving task as directed by the shift supervisor for general operations.


Key Accountabilities


Key accountabilities of this position include.




Safely operate Loader as part of underground work plan pre task jobs.


Bogging of development headings to stockpiles and haul trucks


Conduct regular equipment inspections and report faults


Perform roadworks and manage spillage and sump bogging


Maintain high standards of work quality and safety compliance


Identify and escalate opportunities for operational efficiency


Demonstrate strong safety leadership and environmental awareness.




About You


To be considered for this role, it is essential that you must obtain a minimum qualification of Grade 10 or above with experience in operating underground boggers or teleremotes or similar models. In addition to this, you will have some or all the following.




Must have underground experience with a minimum of 12 months on the bogger, tele remote.


Possess current Class 7 driver’s license.


Must have operating certificate.


Ability to work with close supervision.


Must have Underground Mining experience.


Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.


Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.


Actively promotes a safe and healthy culture.




Life at K92  


K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.


Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.


At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.


In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster. 


THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP 






Apply

About Burnet Institute


Burnet Institute is a leading Australian medical research and public health organization working to achieve better health for vulnerable communities in Australia and internationally. In Papua New Guinea, Burnet has been implementing health research and development programs for almost 20 years, with offices in 
Port Moresby, Kokopo and Western Province
.


About the HEAL-PNG Project


HEAL-PNG is a three-year clinical trial funded by the NHMRC and the Global Alliance for Chronic Diseases (GACD). The project evaluates an innovative model of care that integrates non-communicable disease (NCD) screening and management within existing HIV and TB clinics in 
Morobe
 and
 East New Britain
 provinces. The goal is to improve NCD care through enhanced screening, patient education, adherence support via peer counselling, and simplified management protocols.


About the Role


Lead Counsellors are responsible for providing a range of patient education and counselling services for people on treatment for multiple long-term conditions, which means two or more of the following: diabetes, asthma, cardiovascular disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, HIV, TB.


Additionally, Counsellors facilitate patient referrals, ensuring linkages to various care and support services, and lead peer-support group sessions.


The Lead Counsellor mentors and supports the Peer Counsellors and provides counselling support for people with complex needs, referred by the Peer Counsellors and other staff.


Key Responsibilities




Provide basic educational, emotional and social wellbeing support to people receiving treatment for TB, HIV and other long-term conditions.


Facilitate peer support groups and health education sessions for patients, families and communities.


Work collaboratively with clinical, research, TB and HIV teams to provide person-centred care.


Facilitate referrals to appropriate internal and external health and support services.


Ensure accurate documentation, counselling records, patient information and program data are maintained.


Prepare reports on counselling, patient support and community engagement activities as required.


Support health education and community engagement activities and build effective relationships with relevant services and organisations.


Mentor, support and provide feedback to Peer Counsellors, including assisting with training and professional development.


Participate in case management, adherence and other relevant team meetings.


Participate in ongoing professional development, particularly in counselling, health education and related areas.

Essential:




Minimum 
two years’ experience in counselling or social work
, preferably within a health setting.

.

.

.

28284.description:
About Burnet Institute


Burnet Institute is a leading Australian medical research and public health organization working to achieve better health for vulnerable communities in Australia and internationally. In Papua New Guinea, Burnet has been implementing health research and development programs for almost 20 years, with offices in 
Port Moresby, Kokopo and Western Province
.


About the HEAL-PNG Project


HEAL-PNG is a three-year clinical trial funded by the NHMRC and the Global Alliance for Chronic Diseases (GACD). The project evaluates an innovative model of care that integrates non-communicable disease (NCD) screening and management within existing HIV and TB clinics in 
Morobe
 and
 East New Britain
 provinces. The goal is to improve NCD care through enhanced screening, patient education, adherence support via peer counselling, and simplified management protocols.


About the Role


Lead Counsellors are responsible for providing a range of patient education and counselling services for people on treatment for multiple long-term conditions, which means two or more of the following: diabetes, asthma, cardiovascular disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, HIV, TB.


Additionally, Counsellors facilitate patient referrals, ensuring linkages to various care and support services, and lead peer-support group sessions.


The Lead Counsellor mentors and supports the Peer Counsellors and provides counselling support for people with complex needs, referred by the Peer Counsellors and other staff.


Key Responsibilities




Provide basic educational, emotional and social wellbeing support to people receiving treatment for TB, HIV and other long-term conditions.


Facilitate peer support groups and health education sessions for patients, families and communities.


Work collaboratively with clinical, research, TB and HIV teams to provide person-centred care.


Facilitate referrals to appropriate internal and external health and support services.


Ensure accurate documentation, counselling records, patient information and program data are maintained.


Prepare reports on counselling, patient support and community engagement activities as required.


Support health education and community engagement activities and build effective relationships with relevant services and organisations.


Mentor, support and provide feedback to Peer Counsellors, including assisting with training and professional development.


Participate in case management, adherence and other relevant team meetings.


Participate in ongoing professional development, particularly in counselling, health education and related areas.




Qualifications and Experience


Essential:




Minimum 
two years’ experience in counselling or social work
, preferably within a health setting.


Strong knowledge of, or personal lived experience with, 
TB, HIV or non-communicable diseases
.


Demonstrated 
compassion, empathy and strong interpersonal and communication skills
.


Experience in 
leadership, team supervision and reporting
.


Ability to work independently and demonstrate strong 
judgement, decision-making and problem-solving skills
.


Strong 
organisation and time management skills
.


Demonstrated ability to 
role model positive and respectful behaviour
 within the community.


Basic to intermediate 
computer literacy
, including Microsoft Office.


Ability to 
communicate effectively in Tok Pisin
.




Desirable:




A 
qualification in counselling, education, health, social work or a related field
.


Experience working with 
TB, HIV or non-communicable disease programs
.


Experience facilitating 
health education, peer support or community engagement activities
.


Experience 
mentoring or supervising peer counsellors or community-based staff
.


Additional training in 
counselling, psychosocial support or health promotion




Other Requirements




Compliance with Burnet Institute’s occupational health, safety and safeguarding standards.


Police Check and Working with Children Check (as applicable).

cover letter and current CV

28258.description:
General Manager / Papua New Guinea Country Head
 


MC Infrastructure | Port Moresby
 


MC Infrastructure is looking for a motivated, capable and experienced General Manager to lead our multidisciplinary team in Port Moresby.
 


This role suits someone who enjoys bringing people together, keeping projects moving and creating a positive, accountable workplace. You will initially manage 8 team members working across civil engineering, geotechnical services, environmental consulting, land surveying, planning and project support. Our ambition is to double the size of this team over the next two years.
 


People leadership is the main requirement. A civil engineering, construction project management, geotechnical or environmental background would be advantageous, although we welcome applicants from other relevant professional backgrounds.
 


 


Your responsibilities
 




Provide daily leadership, direction and support to the Port Moresby team
 






Manage client projects in Microsoft Planner and coordinate project delivery across several technical disciplines
 






Coordinate and ensure timely issuance of fee proposals and maintain CRM records 
 






Mentor staff and build a positive and productive workplace culture
 






Set clear priorities, allocate work and monitor deadlines
 






Hold regular team meetings and follow up agreed actions
 






Proactively communicate with and involve senior management
 






Build strong client relationships, ask questions and identify issues early
 






Monitor workloads, project progress, budgets and staff performance
 






Recruit, onboard and support new team members
 






Prepare clear weekly reports for senior management
 






Improve office systems, communication and accountability
 






Promote quality, responsibility and consistent delivery
 




 


About you
 


You will have:
 




Experience leading a team of at least 5 staff
 






Experience recruiting, selecting and onboarding team members
 






Excellent written and verbal communication skills
 






Strong client relationship and stakeholder management experience
 






A practical, organised and solutions-focused approach
 






Confidence setting expectations and holding people accountable
 






Good project coordination and reporting skills
 






Strong computer skills and confidence with modern workplace software
 






Sound judgement and the ability to manage competing priorities
 






A professional background in engineering, construction, environmental science, planning, surveying, geotechnical services or a related field
 




Civil engineering or project management qualifications or experience would be advantageous, but they are not essential. Leadership ability, communication and personal drive will receive greater weight.
 


 


About us
 


MC Infrastructure is part of Pacific Infrastructure Group, a multi-disciplinary consulting group with a focus on building better communities through responsible development. Other divisions within the group include Redbox Design, a Canberra based urban planning and landscape architecture practice and JRK surveys, a Sydney based surveying firm. 
 


MC Infrastructure is the primary civil engineering arm of Pacific Infrastructure Group and has been operating in Papua New Guinea for close to 20 years. In that time, the firm has worked on numerous key infrastructure projects including the design of sustainable community developments and key transport infrastructure.
 


 


What we offer
 




A key leadership role within our Papua New Guinea business with autonomy to create a meaningful impact on the business and its employees
 






The opportunity to influence how the Port Moresby office operates
 






Opportunity to influence the future of linear and non-linear infrastructure, as well as community development in PNG and the South Pacific 
 






A broad range of infrastructure, development and environmental projects
 






Direct support from senior management in Australia
 






Opportunities for professional growth and future management responsibility within the larger group
 






A competitive salary based on experience
 




The position is based full-time in Port Moresby.
 


 


How to Apply


To apply, please submit your CV and a short cover letter to 
[email protected]
 describing the teams you have led, your recruitment experience, your approach to staff leadership and an example of how you managed an important client relationship.
 


 
We are interested in hearing from individual applicants only, and kindly request that recruiters, agencies, and offshore firms refrain from applying.
 


* MCI is committed to equal employment opportunities and does not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment based on factors such as race, colour, religion, national origin, age, gender, sex, ancestry, citizenship status, mental or physical disability, genetic information, sexual orientation, veteran status, or military status. If you are legally able to work with us, we encourage you to apply. We actively seek individuals to join our team and 
do not engage
 with recruiters, agencies, or offshore firms in our hiring process.
 








Apply

28141.description:
PNG Air, renowned for its extensive network covering over 26 destinations throughout Papua New Guinea, operates the largest fleet of ATR 72-600 & ATR 42-600 series aircraft in the region. As the Airline of Choice, we're committed to delivering a world-class experience with competitive fares, unparalleled cargo rates, and a focus on safety and on-time performance for our valued customers and stakeholders.


 


PSS & DCS Manager


 


PNG Air is seeking a suitably qualified and experienced 
PSS & DCS Manager 
to join its Commercial Department based in Port Moresby.


 


Reporting to the 
General Manager – Commercial
, the 
PSS & DCS Manager 
is responsible for the effective implementation, operation, support and continuous improvement of PNG Air's Passenger Service System (PSS), Departure Control System (DCS) and any other systems that fall under the department's remit. The role leads a dedicated team comprising a Team Leader – Helpdesk, Head of Trainers, Helpdesk Officers and Trainers, ensuring all users across the business are well supported and appropriately trained.


The position is the department's owner of process, policy and quality assurance: it designs and maintains the PSS/DCS (and other systems) Process & Policy Manual, holds overall accountability for the QA and standards framework, and is the final approver of all user access requests to these systems.


The PSS & DCS Manager works closely with the General Manager – Commercial, the Head of Training, IT, and PSS/DCS vendors to ensure systems, processes, documentation and training remain fit for purpose and aligned to PNG Air's operational and commercial objectives.


 


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES


Systems Management




Manage the day-to-day operation, configuration and availability of PNG Air's Passenger Service System (PSS) and Departure Control System (DCS).


Act as the primary business owner and subject matter expert for the PSS and DCS platforms, including reservations, inventory, fares, check-in and departure control functions.


Coordinate system upgrades, patches, releases and new functionality with the vendor(s) and internal IT, and oversee user acceptance testing prior to deployment.


Monitor system performance and availability, escalating and managing resolution of outages or degraded service with vendors and IT.




Process, Policy & Quality Assurance




Design, structure and own the PSS & DCS Process and Policy Manual, covering PSS, DCS and any other system that comes under the department's responsibility.


Hold overall accountability for the department's QA and standards framework, setting the standards that the Head of Trainers is responsible for maintaining day to day.


Review and formally approve updates to the Process and Policy Manual, training materials and standard operating procedures before they are published.


Ensure the manual and associated procedures reflect current vendor functionality, IATA requirements and internal audit findings.


Periodically audit adherence to documented processes and standards across the Helpdesk and Training teams.




Helpdesk & User Support




Lead and manage the PSS/DCS Helpdesk function through the Team Leader – Helpdesk, ensuring timely and effective support to all users of PSS and DCS across the network.


Act as final approver of all user access requests to PSS, DCS and related systems, reviewing and confirming access recommended by the Team Leader – Helpdesk.


Establish and monitor helpdesk service levels (response and resolution times) and escalation paths.


Provide a point of escalation for complex or high-priority incidents affecting check-in, boarding or reservations.




Training & Capability Development




Lead and manage the PSS/DCS Training function through the Head of Trainers, ensuring training is planned, delivered and recorded across the network.


Approve the training curricula, manuals and competency assessments maintained by the Head of Trainers.


Ensure training content and standards remain aligned with the guidance of the (external) Head of Training and with current airline, IATA and regulatory requirements.




Vendor & Stakeholder Management




Act as the key liaison with PSS and DCS vendors and service providers, managing service level agreements, support contracts and issue escalation.


Work closely with Commercial, Airport Operations, Call Centre, IT, Revenue Accounting and other departments to ensure PSS/DCS systems, processes and documentation support business needs.


Represent PNG Air in vendor user groups, industry forums and system enhancement discussions relevant to PSS/DCS.




Reporting & Continuous Improvement




Provide regular reporting on helpdesk performance, training completion, user access activity, system incidents and outstanding issues to the General Manager – Commercial.


Identify opportunities to improve system efficiency, reduce manual processes, and enhance the user experience of PSS and DCS.


Support the implementation of new modules, interfaces or automation initiatives across PSS and DCS.




Leadership




Lead, coach and develop the PSS & DCS team, including the Team Leader – Helpdesk, Head of Trainers, Helpdesk Officers and Trainers, fostering a culture of service, accuracy and continuous improvement.


Allocate work, set performance expectations and conduct performance reviews for all direct reports.


Promote collaboration between the Helpdesk and Training functions and across the wider Commercial division.




 


QUALIFICATIONS/EXPERIENCES


 


Essential




Bachelor's Degree in Information Technology, Business, Aviation Management or a related field, or equivalent industry experience.


Minimum three years' experience working with airline Passenger Service Systems (PSS) and/or Departure Control Systems (DCS).


Demonstrated experience leading a team, including helpdesk or training functions.


Demonstrated experience developing or owning process, policy or procedure documentation.


Strong analytical, reporting and problem-solving skills.


Excellent verbal and written communication skills.




 


Desirable




Experience within the aviation industry, in a commercial, airport operations or IT systems role.


Experience delivering systems training or developing training materials.


Familiarity with IATA reservations, ticketing and departure control standards.


Experience managing vendor relationships and service level agreements.


Experience with user access governance or IT/system audit requirements.




 


 


 


 


 


If you feel you meet our requirements and are interested, we would like to hear from you. Send your application in only one PDF file to:


 


[email protected]


 


Applications close: 
Friday 25th September 2026


Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.


 


We are an equal opportunity employer.








Apply

ABOUT KTF:


 


KTF is an Australian international aid and development organisation working in Papua New Guinea (PNG).


 


We work with people and communities to improve the lives and futures of Papua New Guineans. We do this by: assisting remote and rural communities with access to elementary and primary 
education
;
 improving access to quality and accessible 
healthcare
;
 improving 
equality
 
and access to sustainable income-generation opportunities, especially for women; and by fostering the next generation of 
leaders
.


 


KTF is a member of the Australian Council for International Development and is accredited with the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade’s Australian Not-for-Profit Cooperation Program.


 


ABOUT THE ROLE:


This is a short-term, three-month position supporting the FODE program through to the end of 2026. The role will provide additional capacity during a busy period of student records processing, end-of-year administration and program activity.


 


The Student Records and Data Assistant will support the review, verification and maintenance of student education records and supporting documentation. This includes checking digitised student records against original source documents, correcting clear data-entry errors, identifying missing or inconsistent information, and maintaining accurate records of work completed.


 


The role will also provide general administrative support to the FODE team, including invoice and payment processing, maintaining administrative records, and assisting with other program administration tasks as required.


 


The work is detailed and requires exceptional attention to accuracy, good computer skills, strong organisation and the ability to work independently. The position works closely with KTF’s FODE teams and directly supports the effective delivery of FODE Centres and services to students.


 


RESPONSIBILITIES:




Review digitised student certificates, Statements of Results and other education records against original source documentation.


Verify that student names, dates, schools, subjects, grades and other recorded information have been captured accurately.


Correct clear transcription or data-entry errors where source documentation provides definitive evidence.


Classify and reclassify documents in accordance with KTF procedures and approved document categories.


Cross-check records against existing student information to identify duplicates, missing documentation and inconsistencies.


Maintain accurate records of documents reviewed, corrections made, outstanding issues and items requiring follow-up.


Escalate incomplete, conflicting or ambiguous records with clear supporting notes.


Apply KTF data-entry, formatting, naming and document-management standards consistently.


Maintain the confidentiality and security of student information and records.


Assist with the processing and recording of invoices, payments and associated documentation.


Support routine FODE administrative tasks, including maintaining records, preparing information, following up documentation and assisting with administrative processes as required.


Report on progress against agreed work priorities and deadlines.


Participate in regular team meetings and maintain effective communication with relevant KTF staff.


Undertake other data entry, records and administration duties reasonably required within the scope of the role.


Comply with all KTF safeguarding policies, procedures and codes of conduct.




 


SKILLS & ATTRIBUTES:




Exceptional attention to detail and demonstrated accuracy when working with data and records.


Good computer literacy, including confident use of spreadsheets and web-based systems.


Strong personal organisation and the ability to manage a high volume of detailed work while maintaining accuracy.


Ability to follow established processes and apply rules consistently.


Good written and verbal communication skills.


Ability to work independently with minimal day-to-day supervision and contribute effectively as part of a team.


Ability to accurately process and maintain basic financial and administrative records, including invoices and payment documentation.


Familiarity with the PNG education system and secondary school certification, or a strong willingness and ability to learn.


Previous experience in data entry, records administration, finance administration or a similar detail-focused role is desirable.


Willingness to be based in Port Moresby or Balimo and eligibility to work in PNG.

28489.description:
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.


About Lihir


Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.


We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.


Purpose
The Mechanical Advisor is the circuit’s field based technical specialist, providing hands on support to maintenance crews by ensuring work is performed safely, accurately, and to OEM and engineering standards. This role is deeply embedded in day to day execution—conducting inspections, validating defects, troubleshooting equipment issues, and ensuring quality repairs that prevent repeat failures. The Technical Advisor delivers critical technical insights that improve reliability and supports the development of accurate work scopes, plans, and corrective actions. This position is ideal for a technically skilled individual who thrives in the field and is passionate about raising maintenance quality, eliminating defects, and keeping the plant running at its best.


Essential Duties




Field based technical specialist supporting trades.


Field technical quality & defect identification.


On the job technical support, inspections, troubleshooting, failure mode detection.


Conducts inspections and identifies detailed defects.


Raises notifications based on field findings.


Provides field technical detail for task lists, steps, materials, and QA/QC.


Advises on technical schedule readiness and constraints.


Supports technical quality on the job.


Ensures tolerances, standards, and methods are correct.


Provides technical detail on failures and measurements (CM data).


Provides technical analysis input and failure information.


Assists with BI and KPI evaluation.


Provides technical leadership in the field.




Training & Experience




Demonstrated experience in a similar role within the heavy industry


Experience conducting inspections, validating defects, troubleshooting equipment issues, and ensuring quality repairs that prevent repeat failures


Technical leadership field experience


A valid drivers license




Working Conditions
This is a FIFO role on a 21/21 roster.


At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.


We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!






Apply

28488.description:
Newmont produces metals the world needs - safely, responsibly and with care for people, communities and the environment. With a 100+ year history, we continue to shape the future of mining through innovation and strong operational performance. By joining our inclusive, world-class team, you can help shape the future of mining and make a meaningful difference.


Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.


Purpose
The 
Electrical Design Engineer
 will be responsible for delivering electrical design works, plant modifications, design risk assessments, design programs, engineering calculations, document management and red line drawings across the process plant and associated mine site infrastructure.


Working closely with multidisciplinary teams, they will ensure all solutions meet company specifications, operational requirements, contractual obligations, and relevant Australian standards.


Essential Duties




Develop electrical engineering designs and design documentation for mining and process plant infrastructure.


Prepare single-line diagrams, schematics, cable schedules, equipment specifications, and detailed design packages.


Perform power system studies, including load flow, fault level, protection coordination, and arc flash assessments.


Design and review HV and LV power distribution systems, motor control centres (MCCs), substations, switchrooms, and associated infrastructure.


Ensure all designs comply with relevant Australian Standards, statutory requirements, and company engineering standards.


Provide technical support throughout project execution, commissioning, and operational handover phases.


Participate in design reviews, HAZOPs, risk assessments, and constructability workshops.


Coordinate with mechanical, process, instrumentation, and project teams to deliver integrated engineering solutions.


Identify opportunities to improve plant reliability, safety, maintainability, and operational efficiency.


Support site-based modifications and continuous improvement initiatives.




Training & Experience




Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering.


Prior experience of electrical design engineering experience within the mining, minerals processing, or heavy industrial sector.


Demonstrated experience delivering electrical designs for process plants, mine infrastructure, or industrial facilities.


Strong knowledge of AS 3000 and industry regulations relating to electrical engineering design.


Experience with HV and LV power systems, protection systems, motor control, and electrical equipment selection.


Proficiency with industry-standard engineering and design software.


Experience supporting project delivery through design, procurement, construction, and commissioning phases.


Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.


Eligibility for or current membership with Engineers Australia is highly regarded.


Previous site experience within mining operations will be advantageous.




Working Conditions
This is a FIFO role on a 21/21 roster.


At Newmont, our people are our strength and we’re committed to a safe, inclusive and supportive workplace. If you’re passionate about doing work that matters, join Newmont and help shape the future of mining.​


Learn more about our purpose and values: About Newmont​
Hear from our people: Life at Newmont​

POSITION SUMMARY


The Accounts Supervisor (Receivables) is responsible for supervising revenue auditing and accounts receivable activities to ensure all hotel revenues are accurately recorded, reconciled, reported, and collected. This role supports the Director of Finance in maintaining strong financial controls, ensuring compliance with company policies, and safeguarding hotel assets.


The position requires close collaboration with Front Office, Food & Beverage, Sales & Events, Housekeeping, and other operational departments to ensure revenue streams are accurately captured and reflected in the financial records.


 


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES




Verify and reconcile daily hotel revenues to ensure accuracy and completeness.


Review revenue reports, financial records, and system interfaces (Opera PMS, MICROS POS, and General Ledger).


Monitor and investigate revenue discrepancies, unusual transactions, and account variances.


Manage accounts receivable processes, including invoicing, collections, and account reconciliations.


Audit revenue-generating areas such as Rooms, Food & Beverage, Banquets, Laundry, Telephone, and Credit Card transactions.


Conduct regular financial control checks and ensure compliance with company policies and procedures.


Prepare financial, audit, and management reports and assist with month-end closing activities.


Maintain accurate accounting records and ensure compliance with Marriott standards and PNG regulatory requirements.


Supervise and support finance team members, providing guidance and ensuring timely completion of tasks.


Work closely with operational departments to resolve billing and revenue-related issues.


Promote workplace health, safety, security, and compliance with company policies.




 


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS




Diploma or Bachelor's Degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field.


Minimum 2-3 years' experience in Accounts Receivable, Revenue Audit, Finance, or Hotel Accounting.


Previous supervisory or team leadership experience preferred.


Knowledge of hotel financial systems, including Opera PMS, MICROS POS, and General Ledger systems.


Strong understanding of accounting principles, reconciliations, revenue controls, and financial reporting.


Knowledge of PNG GST requirements and financial compliance standards is advantageous.


Strong analytical, problem-solving, and attention-to-detail skills.


Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel.


Excellent communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills.


Ability to work collaboratively across departments and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

28484.description:
POSITION TITLE:
 
MIDWIFE SUPERVISOR– Banz Jiwaka Province


CONTEXT


Médecins Sans Frontières (Doctors Without Borders) is a private, non-profit international humanitarian organization, founded in 1971 and working in 70 countries around the world. MSF provides medical assistance to populations in crisis, regardless of race, religion, belief, or political affiliation. In PNG, MSF has been working since 2007 in Lae, Tari, Bougainville, Gulf Province, and NCD Province. MSF is now working to support the Department of Health to improve access to care for patients in JIWAKA and LAE.


 


JOB PROFILE:  


REPORTING LINE :
  Project Medical Referent, MSF JIWAKA PROJECT


Supervising the clinical activities and guaranteeing the quality of midwifery care in the department, according to 
MSF
 protocols , values and universal hygiene standards in order to provide a high quality Mother and Child Health (MCH) care to the population.




Supervising, supporting and evaluating the team under his/her responsibility particularly midwives, midwife assistants and other related staff in her team such as cleaners. Planning and organizing their work (areas, days, absences, visits, holidays, etc) and coaching them in their work with special focus in following all appropriate protocols and procedures


Ensuring teamwork and a professional relationship between maternity and other departments.


Supervising the clinical activities in all the maternity departments and activities such as ante-natal consultations, delivery and after delivery follow up, post-natal consultations, family planning consultations, new-born vaccinations and liaising with the Medical Doctor about the patients who need special care times, visiting hours, etc.


Ensuring that the staff on duty knows, implements and follows at all times the universal hygiene standards/ precautions, bio-hazard prevention and infection control in the medical premises ensuring high standards of hygiene in the working environment


Ensuring that all staff using medical devices are qualified and trained, cleaning and minor maintenance tasks are performed according to the protocols, reporting any malfunction to the project biomedical service.


Being responsible for the department-related pharmacy activities (stock and consumption monitoring) as well as maintenance of the medical equipment


Being responsible for ensuring that all the administrative procedures, patients’ data and documents are filled in correctly and registered for compiling monthly reports reflecting the activity in the department.


In certain contexts, being responsible for ensuring that the maternity staff is able to identify, receive and provide care to the victims of the SGBV in collaboration with the Obs & Gyne MD and following the protocols.




Generally, to oversee the implementation and quality of sexual violence program and SRH services in all Family Support Centre (FSC) while working together with Jiwaka Provincial Health Authority staff and in conjunction with the Project Medical Referent.


 


Supervision and Staff Support at FSC




Providing supervision to improve quality of clinical activities related to SGBV and SRH care activities (FP, STI & SAC) at the FSC.


Training, coaching, supporting and evaluating the team under her responsibility, following all appropriate protocols and procedures. Training is identified and discussed among the team to ensure they are needed.


Ensuring teamwork and a professional relationship between the Family Support Centre and other departments.




 


Documentation and Reporting




Ensure that all administrative procedures and documents are completed correctly according to the National guidelines and/or MSF Guidelines, whichever is applicable.


Compiling and analyzing monthly reports


Ensure that the confidentiality of any survivor of violence is kept in a locked cupboard to ensure their information is securely stored.


Participate in the weekly medical meeting and monthly reporting and discussion of the project.




 


Pharmacy Management and Logistics Coordination




Responsible for overall pharmacy management at FSC (stocks availability, consumption monitoring, inventory, and re-order) as well as maintenance of medical equipment.


Coordinate with the logistic team in planning movement activity and other logistic support for the activity.




 


Interdepartmental Collaboration




Being responsible for ensuring that the FSC staff can identify, receive and provide care to the survivors of SGBV including other reproductive health concerns in collaboration with the Mental Health team, HP team, and other stakeholders (e.g., police, social services, legal services) to ensure a holistic and integrated approach.


Support other medical team members in their activities, e.g., HP team in building the capacity of the Community Health Workers (CHWs) and Village Health Volunteers (VHVs) in Jiwaka villages, on identification of survivors outside of the health center and referral pathway.


Collaborate with the Officer In Charge (OIC) and health centre staff, organize training for nurses, health extension officers (HEOs), HP officers and CHWs to identify survivors during their medical consultation/ANC/PNC. After the training, follow up with trainees in their daily consultation with the patients through coaching.


Schedule feedback and update meetings with the OIC and health centre staff.




 


SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS










 












Local language essential (Tok Pidgin), knowledge of mission language (English)


Key competencies: commitment, flexibility, results-oriented, stress management, and teamwork, Reliability, discipline, and respect for procedures are critical behavioral competencies.


Registered Nurse/Midwife (diploma essential) with at least 
2 years
 of experience as Midwife.


Having Valid License issued by 
PNG Nursing Council
.


Essential working experience with 
PHA
 and 
Government Health facility
 .


Desirable experience in 
MSF
 or other 
INGOs, NGOs. 
 


Essential computer literacy (word, excel, PowerPoint, internet, outlook).


Strict adherence to MSF policies, including zero tolerance for alcohol consumption during working hours.




 










 


WORKING CONDITIONS
 




Full-time position with an open-ended contract.


Based in Banz, Jiwaka Province with frequent visits to project areas (Family Support Centers, Health Posts & Health Centers) in Jiwaka Province.


Candidates must be flexible with working hours and location.




 


APPLICATION PROCESS

Cover letter
 with an 
updated CV
 and a copy of any other relevant documents

,

Work Certificates

Reference Letter
s) to:

 for the written tests and interviews. Written tests and interviews will be held in Banz, Jiwaka Province.

28457.description:
Newmont produces metals the world needs - safely, responsibly and with care for people, communities and the environment. With a 100+ year history, we continue to shape the future of mining through innovation and strong operational performance. By joining our inclusive, world-class team, you can help shape the future of mining and make a meaningful difference.


 


Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.


 


We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.


 










Your Impact






As an Advisor People Training (Mining), you'll develop and deliver training programs, coach and assess personnel, and support capability development across heavy equipment operations including haul trucks, auxiliary equipment and loading equipment. You'll help ensure employees are trained to contribute to safe production outcomes by identifying skill gaps, adapting training programs and promoting proactive safety behaviours.










As part of our team, you will








Develop training materials and deliver training aligned with Newmont, industry and HSE standards for heavy equipment operations.


Deliver both theory and on-the-job training for operators across mine operations, including haul truck, excavator and loader training.


Conduct field observations and engage with operational leaders to identify capability gaps and enhance training programs.


Maintain accurate training records within the Learning Management System (LMS) and communicate training plans with key stakeholders.


Promote safe and productive work practices while supporting continuous improvement and development across the workforce












Prerequisites for your success in this role








Considerable experience in an open pit mining operation as an operator, supervisor or trainer, with demonstrated capability across heavy equipment operations.


Certificate IV Training and Assessment or equivalent professional education and training qualification.


Subject matter expertise in haul trucks, loading equipment, auxiliary equipment and operational mining training practices.


Experience developing training materials and curricula, delivering classroom and field-based training, and applying adult learning principles.


Strong computer skills including Microsoft Office and Learning Management Systems (LMS), supported by effective communication and stakeholder engagement skills.












Your work environment






This role is offered on a 21:21 Fly-in, Fly-out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea.


Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp environment, with ensuite, air-conditioned accommodation equipped with a mini fridge, television and Wi-Fi. A variety of nutritious meal options are available through the on-site catering facilities, while recreational and social amenities provide opportunities to relax and connect with colleagues while on roster.


Reporting to the Team Lead, Mine Training and working closely with Mine Production Supervisors and the Technical Training team. YOu'll collaborate with operational supervisors, superintendents and other stakeholders to support workforce capability development and training outcomes.










Why join Newmont






Lihir is one of the world's largest producing gold mines and one of Newmont's most significant operations.


Working at Lihir means joining a high-performing team committed to safety, operational excellence and delivering sustainable value for our people, communities and business. 


Eligible employees may benefit from:
•    Competitive salary and annual performance incentive opportunities.
•    Company-funded FIFO travel and modern camp accommodation.
•    Access to health, wellbeing and employee assistance programs.
•    Ongoing learning, technical development and leadership training opportunities.
•    Exposure to large-scale mining operations and industry-leading technologies.
•    Career opportunities across Newmont's Australian, Papua New Guinean and global operations.
•    Access to a diverse range of on-site recreational, dining and wellbeing facilities.
•    The opportunity to be part of a workplace where safety, inclusion and growth are at the centre of everything we do. 


Submit your application through our website quoting reference number 44631 before the advertised closing date: 23 September 2026.












At Newmont, our people are our strength and we’re committed to a safe, inclusive and supportive workplace. If you’re passionate about doing work that matters, join Newmont and help shape the future of mining.​






Learn more about our purpose and values: 
About Newmont
​
Hear from our people: 
Life at Newmont
​






Important: Newmont does not ask candidates to pay money or share sensitive personal data outside our secure application process. If this happens, please report it to our Business Integrity team: 
[email protected]
.

28441.description:
SENIOR OFFICER - GENDER EQUALITY, DISABILITY AND SOCIAL INCLUSION (GEDSI) & 
MONITORING EVALUATION AND LEARNING (MEL)


 


The Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) is an international non-governmental organisation committed to working with communities, government, and other partners to manage wildlife and wild places for biodiversity and human well-being.


WCS PNG seeks a dynamic 
Senior
 
Officer
 
in Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) & Monitoring Evaluation Learning (MEL) 
to ensure conservation initiatives are inclusive, equitable, evidence-based, and responsive to the needs of women, men, youth, persons with disabilities, and other marginalized groups. Reporting to the Senior Community Relations Manager, the position is full-time and based in Goroka, Eastern Highlands Province.


Main Responsibilities: 


 


Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI)




Lead the implementation of Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) strategies across terrestrial conservation projects.


Ensure GEDSI principles are integrated into project planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, and reporting.


Conduct gender, disability, and social inclusion assessments to identify barriers, risks, and opportunities for inclusive conservation programming.


Facilitate inclusive community consultations and awareness activities that promote meaningful participation of women, youth, persons with disabilities, and marginalized groups.


Build the capacity of WCS staff, Community Engagement Officers, Community Facilitators, and local partners on GEDSI principles, safeguarding, and inclusive community engagement.


Support the development and implementation of safeguarding, social inclusion, and community feedback and grievance mechanisms.


Ensure Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC) processes and community consultations are inclusive and culturally appropriate.


Develop partnerships with government agencies, civil society organizations, Disabled Persons Organisations (DPOs), women's organizations, and other stakeholders to strengthen inclusive conservation.


Monitor GEDSI indicators and contribute to organizational learning by documenting lessons learned, success stories, and best practices.




 


Monitoring and Evaluation (MEL)




Support the implementation of project Monitoring and Evaluation (MEL) frameworks and annual monitoring of reports and work plans.


Develop and maintain simple project monitoring databases and data management systems.


Coordinate routine collection, verification, storage, and analysis of project reports in the database.


Conduct regular field monitoring visits to assess implementation progress, verify outputs, and monitor project performance.


Support baseline surveys, community assessments, outcome monitoring, and project evaluations.


Simple analyse quantitative and qualitative monitoring data and prepare summaries for project management and decision-making.


Work Closely with senior WCS staff to prepare monthly, quarterly, annual, and donor monitoring reports in accordance with WCS and donor requirements.




 


Other Responsibilities




Support project design, proposal development, and donor reporting.


Provide technical support to Community Engagement Officers and project teams on GEDSI and basic M&E.


Represent WCS at GEDSI, safeguarding, monitoring, and learning meetings where appropriate.


Perform any other duties assigned by the Senior Community Relations Manager and Senior Terrestrial Conservation Manager.




 


 


Minimum Requirements:




Bachelor's Degree in Community Development Studies, Environmental Management, Natural Resource Management, Agriculture, Public Administration, Monitoring and Evaluation, or another relevant discipline.


Postgraduate qualifications in Gender, Monitoring and Evaluation, Development Studies, or a related discipline will be an advantage.




 


Experience




Minimum five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in Gender Equality and Social Inclusion, community development, monitoring and evaluation, or international development.


Experience integrating GEDSI into community-based conservation or rural development programs.


Capable of working with customary landowners and rural communities in Papua New Guinea.


Experience in designing and implementing monitoring systems and collecting field data.


Has experience in preparing donor reports and project performance reports.


Ability to conduct community consultations, gender assessments, and participatory research.


Previously worked with NGOs, government agencies, donor-funded projects, and community-based organizations.


Proficiency in using digital data collection tools (e.g., KoboToolbox, ODK, Survey123, or similar) will be an advantage.




 


Critical Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities




Strong knowledge of Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) principles.


Good understanding of safeguarding and protection principles.


Strong understanding of Monitoring and Evaluation concepts, indicators, data collection methodologies, and reporting.


Knowledge of community-based conservation and participatory development approaches.


Good understanding of Papua New Guinea's customary land tenure and governance systems.


Strong facilitation, presentation, and training skills.


Excellent interpersonal and stakeholder engagement skills.


Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving abilities.


Excellent report writing and communication skills in English and Tok Pisin.


Experience using Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.


Experience using basic data analysis software and digital data collection platforms is desirable.


Ability to work independently and collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams.


Willingness to travel extensively to remote field locations under basic field conditions.


High integrity, professionalism, cultural sensitivity, and commitment to inclusive conservation and evidence-based decision making.

28431.description:
TITLE:
 
MIDWIFE SUPERVISOR– Banz Jiwaka Province


CONTEXT


Médecins Sans Frontières (Doctors Without Borders) is a private, non-profit international humanitarian organization, founded in 1971 and working in 70 countries around the world. MSF provides medical assistance to populations in crisis, regardless of race, religion, belief, or political affiliation. In PNG, MSF has been working since 2007 in Lae, Tari, Bougainville, Gulf Province, and NCD Province. MSF is now working to support the Department of Health to improve access to care for patients in JIWAKA and LAE.


 


JOB PROFILE:  


REPORTING LINE :
  Project Medical Referent, MSF JIWAKA PROJECT


Supervising the clinical activities and guaranteeing the quality of midwifery care in the department, according to 
MSF
 protocols , values and universal hygiene standards in order to provide a high quality Mother and Child Health (MCH) care to the population.




Supervising, supporting and evaluating the team under his/her responsibility particularly midwives, midwife assistants and other related staff in her team such as cleaners. Planning and organizing their work (areas, days, absences, visits, holidays, etc) and coaching them in their work with special focus in following all appropriate protocols and procedures


Ensuring teamwork and a professional relationship between maternity and other departments.


Supervising the clinical activities in all the maternity departments and activities such as ante-natal consultations, delivery and after delivery follow up, post-natal consultations, family planning consultations, new-born vaccinations and liaising with the Medical Doctor about the patients who need special care times, visiting hours, etc.


Ensuring that the staff on duty knows, implements and follows at all times the universal hygiene standards/ precautions, bio-hazard prevention and infection control in the medical premises ensuring high standards of hygiene in the working environment


Ensuring that all staff using medical devices are qualified and trained, cleaning and minor maintenance tasks are performed according to the protocols, reporting any malfunction to the project biomedical service.


Being responsible for the department-related pharmacy activities (stock and consumption monitoring) as well as maintenance of the medical equipment


Being responsible for ensuring that all the administrative procedures, patients’ data and documents are filled in correctly and registered for compiling monthly reports reflecting the activity in the department.


In certain contexts, being responsible for ensuring that the maternity staff is able to identify, receive and provide care to the victims of the SGBV in collaboration with the Obs & Gyne MD and following the protocols.




Generally, to oversee the implementation and quality of sexual violence program and SRH services in all Family Support Centre (FSC) while working together with Jiwaka Provincial Health Authority staff and in conjunction with the Project Medical Referent.


 


Supervision and Staff Support at FSC




Providing supervision to improve quality of clinical activities related to SGBV and SRH care activities (FP, STI & SAC) at the FSC.


Training, coaching, supporting and evaluating the team under her responsibility, following all appropriate protocols and procedures. Training is identified and discussed among the team to ensure they are needed.


Ensuring teamwork and a professional relationship between the Family Support Centre and other departments.




 


Documentation and Reporting




Ensure that all administrative procedures and documents are completed correctly according to the National guidelines and/or MSF Guidelines, whichever is applicable.


Compiling and analyzing monthly reports


Ensure that the confidentiality of any survivor of violence is kept in a locked cupboard to ensure their information is securely stored.


Participate in the weekly medical meeting and monthly reporting and discussion of the project.




 


Pharmacy Management and Logistics Coordination




Responsible for overall pharmacy management at FSC (stocks availability, consumption monitoring, inventory, and re-order) as well as maintenance of medical equipment.


Coordinate with the logistic team in planning movement activity and other logistic support for the activity.




 


Interdepartmental Collaboration




Being responsible for ensuring that the FSC staff can identify, receive and provide care to the survivors of SGBV including other reproductive health concerns in collaboration with the Mental Health team, HP team, and other stakeholders (e.g., police, social services, legal services) to ensure a holistic and integrated approach.


Support other medical team members in their activities, e.g., HP team in building the capacity of the Community Health Workers (CHWs) and Village Health Volunteers (VHVs) in Jiwaka villages, on identification of survivors outside of the health center and referral pathway.


Collaborate with the Officer In Charge (OIC) and health centre staff, organize training for nurses, health extension officers (HEOs), HP officers and CHWs to identify survivors during their medical consultation/ANC/PNC. After the training, follow up with trainees in their daily consultation with the patients through coaching.


Schedule feedback and update meetings with the OIC and health centre staff.




 


SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS










 












Local language essential (Tok Pidgin), knowledge of mission language (English)


Key competencies: commitment, flexibility, results-oriented, stress management, and teamwork, Reliability, discipline, and respect for procedures are critical behavioral competencies.


Registered Nurse/Midwife (diploma essential) with at least 
2 years
 of experience as Midwife.


Having Valid License issued by 
PNG Nursing Council
.


Essential working experience with 
PHA
 and 
Government Health facility
 .


Desirable experience in 
MSF
 or other 
INGOs, NGOs. 
 


Essential computer literacy (word, excel, PowerPoint, internet, outlook).


Strict adherence to MSF policies, including zero tolerance for alcohol consumption during working hours.




 










 


WORKING CONDITIONS
 




Full-time position with an open-ended contract.


Based in Banz, Jiwaka Province with frequent visits to project areas (Family Support Centers, Health Posts & Health Centers) in Jiwaka Province.


Candidates must be flexible with working hours and location.




 


APPLICATION PROCESS


The applicants must send their 
Cover letter
 with an 
updated CV
 and a copy of any other relevant documents 
(Diplomas

s) to:

 for the written tests and interviews. Written tests and interviews will be held in Banz, Jiwaka Province.
